subject: maths
title: Addition and Subtraction - Doubles and Counting On

steps.title: Double and count on

options.label: Tap the three beans once each. This is our first group.
Double three means three again. Add another group of three beans.
For four plus nine, start with nine. Count on four more beans.

steps.hint: Tap each object once. A marked object has already been counted.
steps.explanation: Add the same group again for doubles; start with the larger number.
steps.shortExplanation: Make, count or compare the objects. Explain what changed.

mathWorkshop.title: Double and count on
mathWorkshop.goal: Add the same group again for doubles; start with the larger number.

tasks.prompt: Tap the three beans once each. This is our first group.
tasks.feedback: Our first group has three beans.
tasks.hint: You counted them all. The last number you said tells how many.

tasks.prompt: Double three means three again. Add another group of three beans.
tasks.feedback: Three and another three make six. Double three is six.
tasks.hint: Keep the first three. Add the same number again.

tasks.prompt: For four plus nine, start with nine. Count on four more beans.
tasks.feedback: Starting at nine and adding four reaches thirteen. Nine plus four equals four plus nine.
tasks.hint: Say ten, eleven, twelve, thirteen as you add four beans.

parentReview.en: Guided practice is ungraded. Completion records the child doing the activities, not a book-question score.

steps.title: Doubles
steps.hint: A double is the same number added again.
steps.explanation: Double means the same number added again.
steps.shortExplanation: Double means the same number added again.

steps.title: Counting on from 8
steps.prompt: Start with the bigger number and find 3 + 8.
steps.hint: Start on 8, the bigger number, and count on 3.
steps.explanation: Start at 8 and count on 3 to reach 11.
steps.shortExplanation: Start at 8 and count on 3 to reach 11.

steps.title: Counting on from 12
steps.prompt: Start with the bigger number and find 5 + 12.
steps.hint: Start on 12, the bigger number, and count on 5.
steps.explanation: Start at 12 and count on 5 to reach 17.
steps.shortExplanation: Start at 12 and count on 5 to reach 17.

steps.title: More birds
steps.prompt: 8 birds are in a tree. 4 more come. How many now?
steps.hint: Start on 8 and count on 4 more.

steps.title: Counting back from 15
steps.hint: Start on 15 and jump back three times.

steps.title: Difference of 13 and 17
steps.prompt: What is the difference between 13 and 17?
steps.hint: Start on 13 and count the jumps to 17.

steps.title: Try it at home
steps.prompt: Tell an adult your own number story for 6 + 4 = 10. Act it out with safe objects.
steps.hint: Start with the bigger number. A double adds the same number again.
steps.explanation: Try it with an adult. Talk about what you found.
steps.shortExplanation: Try it with an adult. Talk about what you found.

source.answerKeyText:
Any story where 6 things and 4 more things are joined to make 10, e.g. "6 cars were
parked, 4 more came, now there are 10."

parentReview.en:
Any story where 6 things and 4 more things are joined to make 10, e.g. "6 cars were
parked, 4 more came, now there are 10."
parentReview.note: Discuss with an adult; this personal or drawing response is not automatically graded.

steps.title: The quickest start
steps.prompt: For 2 + 9, the quickest way is to start counting on from...
steps.explanation: Starting on the bigger number, 9, needs only two jumps.
steps.shortExplanation: Starting on the bigger number, 9, needs only two jumps.

steps.title: Swapping numbers
steps.hint: Does the order of adding change the total?
steps.explanation: Swapping the numbers does not change the total: 3 + 7 is 10 too.
steps.shortExplanation: Swapping the numbers does not change the total: 3 + 7 is 10 too.

steps.title: Taking 2 from 20
steps.hint: Start on 20 and jump back twice.
steps.explanation: Two jumps back from 20 land on 18.
steps.shortExplanation: Two jumps back from 20 land on 18.
